newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade students offer to end marathon protest.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade students offer to end marathon protest.

text.p: Belgrade University students demonstrating against election fraud on Wednesday offered to end their protest and return to classes on Monday if rector Dragutin Velickovic steps down.
Protesting students will return to their faculties for two hours on Friday morning, protest organisers said.

"If the rector and deputy rector do not submit their resignations during those two hours, the students will go back to the plateau (base of demonstrations) and extend their demands," Tanja Milovanovic, a member of the student protest leadership, told Reuters.
If the rector steps down the students will officially end their protest and resume classes on Monday, she said.
The students plan to march through Belgrade on Thursday, continuing the marathon protest they have maintained for 104 days.

Velickovic on Tuesday angered the students when he refused to bow to their demands and resign. Speaking at a news conference, he instead asked for the dismissal of faculty deans and institute chiefs who have supported the daily student protest.
Angry students occupied his office on Wednesday.
Velickovic has said he will resign only when the students return to classes.
Tiring of the marathon protest with no solution to the impasse in sight, university deans loyal to the students pressed them on Wednesday to test Velickovic's promise by returning to their faculties.

The student protests have continued even after the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition ended three months of mass demonstrations in February after Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic restored local election victories in 14 cities which his ruling socialist party (SPS) annulled in November.
The widespread protests were the biggest challenge to Milosevic's 10-year rule and ended 52 years of communist control of the capital Belgrade when Zajedno leader Zoran Djindjic took over as mayor.
The students carried on marching and demanding the resignation of the rector, a diehard SPS appointee who had condemned their demonstrations for what he sees as siding with his political foes.
But almost four months of daily peaceful and highly imaginative protests appeared to have taken their , resulting in cracks in the unity of the student leaders.

Velickovic's move on Tuesday followed a meeting of the Belgrade University Teaching Board on Sunday when 27 faculty deans out of a total of 30 and chiefs of all eight institutes sided with the students and voted for Velickovic's dismissal.
They elected Dragan Kuburovic as the new university chief in a move Velickovic proclaimed as illegal.
Velickovic's initiative for sacking the rebel deans will be discussed at the University Council which meets when called by Milosevic's government.
Velickovic has refused to budge from his post despite a written agreement by two Serbian deputy prime ministers last December that he would be sacked.
The Serbian government on Wednesday warned it would take unspecified action against the protesters and their professors unless classes resumed.
All opposition leaders and sympathisers have backed the student protests.

Zajedno is preparing fresh protests for Sunday, the 6th anniversary of massive anti-government demonstrations in Belgrade in which two people were killed and which Milosevic quelled with tanks and heavy armour.
